newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Eurofima to grant loan to Yugo railways.
newsitem.headline: Eurofima to grant loan to Yugo railways.

text.p: European society for financing railway rolling stock Eurofima is ready to extend a loan to Yugoslav railways to help it reintegrate into the European railway network, Belgrade daily Politika said Wednesday.
Head of a visiting Eurofima delegation Heinz Weber said the Eurofima Board of Directors will approve a new loan to Yugoslav railways at its meeting early in June.
No specific figures on the size of the loan were given.
Yugoslav railways needs to provide a list of its most urgent needs as soon as possible so that the credit can become operational by mid-June.
The loan will be used to help Yugoslav railways increase efficiency and complete production of new carriages.

"Eurofima's financial support will enable Yugoslav railways to meet standards for joining the European railway network, which will in turn improve its financial position and make it possible to get new loans," Yugoslav transport minister Dejan Drobnjakovic was quoted as saying.
Weber expected Eurofima to approve other credits to Yugoslavia by the end of 1997 to upgrade its railways.
The Eurofima delegation was received by Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic and Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic.

Kontic said Yugoslavia was one of the founders of the Eurofima which had in the past 50 years invested about two billion Swiss francs in the development of railways in the former Yugoslavia of which Serbia and Montenegro received 50 percent of the funds. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom 381 11 222 43 05
